name: Protected Missing Cubes Force USO Cycles
statement: Let $H\subseteq Q_F$ be ample and $S\subseteq H$ have at least two vertices. Suppose that for every $x\in S$ there is a set $J_x\subseteq F$ such that every neighbor $x^{\{e\}}$ with $e\in J_x$ lies in $S$, while the opposite cube vertex $x^{J_x}$ is absent from $H$. Then every USO of $H$, if one exists, contains a directed cycle in $S$. Consequently $H$ is not dismantlable ample.
proof: The outgoing-cube axiom prevents all directions in $J_x$ from pointing outward at $x$, because their joint flip is missing. Thus every vertex of the finite digraph induced by $S$ has an incoming neighbor in $S$. Following predecessors eventually repeats a vertex and produces a directed cycle. Dismantlable ampleness is equivalent to existence of an acyclic USO.
